q: What is a sustainability bond in India and which SEBI rules apply to it?
title: Sustainability bonds under SEBI
short: A sustainability bond funds a mix of eligible green and social projects. SEBI's June 2025 framework makes the issuer meet both rule sets: the green debt disclosures in Chapter IX of the NCS Master Circular and the social bond disclosures in Annexure A, with an independent reviewer and the anti-purpose-washing duties.
audience: Listed companies and NBFCs choosing a sustainable debt label

p: SEBI defines a sustainability bond as a debt security whose proceeds finance or refinance a combination of eligible green projects and social projects, as defined for green debt securities and social bonds respectively. Social bonds, sustainability bonds, sustainability-linked bonds and green debt securities together make up ESG debt securities under Regulation 2(1)(oa) of the NCS Regulations.

SEBI recognises that social projects can have environmental co-benefits and green projects social co-benefits. The issuer decides whether the bond is green, social or sustainability based on the primary objective of the underlying projects.

ul: Everything required for green debt securities: environmental objectives, project eligibility, proceeds tracking, refinancing split, risk mitigation, and post-issue impact reporting and BRSR elements.
Everything required for social bonds: social objectives and target population, social risks, and project-level social impact reporting.
External auditor verification of the use of proceeds, and unutilised money reported per ISIN.
Keep a decision process that checks projects remain eligible.
Make sure every funded project meets the documented objectives and use proceeds only for the stated purpose.
Follow the purpose-washing rules: monitor real impact, quantify negative externalities and never imply a certification that does not exist.

senseible: Senseible supplies energy and emissions records for MSME sites, which can support the green half of impact reporting. It does not review or label bonds.
